Tomato Early Blight.recommended_action: Remove affected leaves and apply the recommended treatment.
Tomato Early Blight.symptoms: Dark concentric rings (target-board spots) on older leaves, yellowing chlorotic halos around lesions, premature leaf drop.
Tomato Early Blight.organicRemedy: Spray Neem oil solution (3-5 ml/L) or Copper soap fungicide every 7 days. Prune heavily infected lower leaves 12 inches above the soil.
Tomato Early Blight.chemicalRemedy: Apply Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2g/liter or Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5g/liter at first sign of target spots.
suggestions: Remove affected leaves immediately and destroy them (do not compost).
Avoid overhead watering; irrigate at the soil level to keep foliage dry.
Apply copper-based fungicide or Neem oil solution (2-3 ml/L) every 7-10 days.
Ensure proper plant spacing for sunlight and air circulation.
Rotate tomato crops with non-solanaceous crops (e.g., maize, beans) next season.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seeds and resistant varieties
Ensure proper plant spacing for air circulation
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation to keep foliage dry
Rotate crops annually with non-solanaceous plants

Potato Late Blight.recommended_action: Prune infected plant parts immediately and apply systemic fungicide (Mancozeb/Ridomil Gold).
Potato Late Blight.symptoms: Water-soaked dark brown/black necrotic lesions on leaf tips, white fungal mold on lower surface during humid weather.
Potato Late Blight.organicRemedy: Prune and destroy infected leaves immediately. Spray bio-fungicide containing Bacillus subtilis or copper octanoate.
Potato Late Blight.chemicalRemedy: Apply Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% (Ridomil Gold) @ 2.5g/liter or Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP.
suggestions: Prune infected plant parts immediately to prevent rapid canopy spore spread.
Apply systemic fungicide containing Mancozeb or Ridomil Gold.
Maintain well-drained soil and avoid standing water.
Monitor daily during high humidity and cool damp nights.
Destroy harvested tubers showing surface brown rot.
prevention: Plant certified blight-free seed tubers
Ensure good field drainage and avoid waterlogging
Destroy crop residues and cull piles post-harvest
Apply preventative copper spray prior to rainy spells

Rice Leaf Blast.recommended_action: Spray Tricyclazole 75 WP @ 0.6 g/L and maintain proper paddy water levels.
Rice Leaf Blast.symptoms: Spindle-shaped or diamond-shaped lesions with grayish-white centers and reddish-brown borders on leaf blades.
Rice Leaf Blast.organicRemedy: Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/L or 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) at early tiller emergence.
Rice Leaf Blast.chemicalRemedy: Spray Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6g/L water or Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5ml/L at first appearance of blast lesions.
suggestions: Avoid excessive nitrogenous fertilizer application.
Maintain 2-5 cm standing water layer in paddy field to reduce spore germ tube entry.
Spray Tricyclazole 75 WP @ 0.6 g/L water at first appearance of lesions.
Select blast-resistant rice cultivars for the next sowing cycle.
prevention: Avoid excess nitrogenous fertilizer (split N applications)
Keep field flooded during tillering stage
Treat seeds with Carbendazim or Tricyclazole before nursery sowing
Plant blast-tolerant regional paddy cultivars

Cotton Bacterial Blight.disease: Cotton Angular Leaf Spot / Bacterial Blight (Xanthomonas citri)
Cotton Bacterial Blight.recommended_action: Spray Streptocycline mixed with Copper Oxychloride and remove infected plant debris.
Cotton Bacterial Blight.symptoms: Angular dark water-soaked spots bounded strictly by leaf veins, progressing to systemic stem black-arm lesions.
Cotton Bacterial Blight.organicRemedy: Spray 5% NSKE (Neem seed kernel extract) and prune diseased twigs during clear dry weather.
Cotton Bacterial Blight.chemicalRemedy: Spray Streptocycline (100 ppm, approx 1g/10L) mixed with Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5g/L water.
suggestions: Spray Streptocycline (100 ppm) mixed with Copper Oxychloride (0.25%).
Use delinted and seed-treated disease-free certified cotton seeds.
Remove infected crop residue from the field post-harvest.
Avoid flood irrigation that carries bacteria between rows.
prevention: Use acid-delinted certified disease-free cotton seeds
Avoid furrow/flood irrigation that spreads bacteria along rows
Deep summer plowing to bury previous crop debris
Maintain wider row spacing for rapid morning leaf drying

Corn Common Rust.recommended_action: Apply foliar fungicide (Mancozeb @ 2g/L) and plant rust-resistant hybrids.
Corn Common Rust.symptoms: Small cinnamon-brown to reddish-orange raised powdery pustules scattered across upper and lower leaf surfaces.
Corn Common Rust.organicRemedy: Dust sulfur powder (25-30 kg/ha) or spray bio-control formulation of Trichoderma viride.
Corn Common Rust.chemicalRemedy: Apply Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1ml/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2g/L if infection exceeds 10% before silking.
suggestions: Apply foliar fungicide (Mancozeb @ 2g/L) if infection occurs before silking stage.
Plant rust-resistant hybrid corn varieties.
Ensure balanced soil potassium levels to improve natural immunity.
prevention: Plant rust-resistant hybrid corn varieties
Destroy infected crop residues after harvest
Maintain optimal plant density for sunlight penetration
Ensure balanced soil potassium to improve natural crop defense

Healthy Leaf.recommended_action: No chemical action required. Maintain regular irrigation, balanced nutrition, and routine scouting.
Healthy Leaf.symptoms: Vibrant green leaf coloration, uniform chlorophyll pigmentation, smooth intact cuticle, no lesions or chlorosis.
Healthy Leaf.organicRemedy: Continue current organic schedule with well-decomposed farmyard manure (FYM) and bio-fertilizers.
Healthy Leaf.chemicalRemedy: No chemical treatment required. Preserve beneficial predatory insects and pollinator populations.
suggestions: Continue regular irrigation and balanced fertilization (NPK).
Monitor weekly for early pest or disease signs.
Maintain optimal field weed control and healthy soil organic carbon.
prevention: Maintain weekly crop scouting
Ensure balanced N-P-K nutrient and micronutrient supply
Keep field borders clean of alternate weed hosts
Practice timely crop rotation
